banned.claim: Beats 'the world's #1 toothpaste brand' as an unqualified named comparison.
banned.why: FTC substantiation - comparative superiority claims must be tied to the specific in-vitro test conditions, not stated as a blanket unqualified superlative.

banned.claim: 'Developed by NASA' as a standalone endorsement.
banned.why: FTC - implies an endorsement/origin not clearly substantiated; NASA does not endorse products, so this needs precise, provable framing.

banned.claim: Guaranteed to whiten, repair, or cure sensitivity for everyone.
banned.why: FTC - no guaranteed-results claims; effects must be presented as typical, not universal outcomes.

banned.claim: 'The best teethcare in the world' or '#1 toothpaste'.
banned.why: FTC - banned unqualified superlatives that cannot be objectively proven.

banned.claim: 'Summer/New-Year exclusive - only hours left' style countdown urgency.
banned.why: FTC - fake or manufactured urgency is prohibited; deadlines must be real.

banned.claim: Citing a specific review count or 4.7/5 rating without verifiable underlying reviews.
banned.why: FTC - invented or unsubstantiated review counts and ratings are banned; must reflect genuine, typical customer feedback.
